passages.context: Morrisroe identifies the credence as a small sanctuary table for service objects and records early-twentieth-century material, dimensional, cloth, side-placement, and Low-Mass variation. The consumer uses only the table identity and evidence that its form and use varied; the article's measurements, material list, cloth prescriptions, and exact location are not generalized.

passages.context: Corbett reports as the 'usual chronology' that David was born in 1085 B.C. and reigned from 1055 to 1015 B.C.; he immediately distinguishes this conventional scheme from recent writers who, influenced by Assyrian inscriptions, dated the reign thirty to fifty years later. This passage supports attribution of the 1055-1015 B.C. reign span to Corbett's named conventional chronology, not its presentation as an exact date supplied by the biblical text or as the encyclopedia's account of modern critical consensus.
